newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Exhausted Hutu refugees walk towards Kisangani.
newsitem.headline: Exhausted Hutu refugees walk towards Kisangani.

text.p: Hundreds of bedraggled Hutu refugees who fled fighting in eastern Zaire were spotted heading west towards the city of Kisangani on Monday, having already walked around 70 km (45 miles) from their camp.
Reporters flown to the area in a Zaire military helicopter from Kisangani saw refugees stretched out along the road about 150 km (100 miles) west of Kisangani in the hundreds.
Some had only one shoe and many leaned on walking sticks with bandages wrapped around their legs.
Most of those who reached that far were aged under 30.

The Hutus said they had fled the camp at Tingi Tingi, formerly home to an estimated 170,000 refugees, on Friday after hearing mortar fire nearby. They said they had little idea where they would be going.

The governor of the Upper Zaire region told reporters the refugees would be diverted off the main road to Kisangani and received at the town of Ubundu around 100 km (60 miles) south of the provincial capital.

"At Kisangani we already have too many problems with the displaced, with the local population, with unemployment, and with food shortages. We will direct the refugees towards Ubundu,' Governor Lombeya Basongo said.
Ubundu, like Kisangani is situated on the banks of the vast Zaire river.
A Western businessman who has visited the town, said it is surrounded by mangroves swamps with little opportunity for refugees to find food.
"It could be the largest cemetery in Zaire," he said.
Refugees trudging down the road towards another unknown destiny, said that they had left behind them the sick and elderly at Tingi Tingi.
Before evacuating the region on Saturday relief workers said that already around 40 of the refugees were dying daily from starvation and disease.
The regional governor accused aid agencies of pulling out for no reason and denied that U.N. and humanitarian personnel had been harassed by Zairean soldiers and foreign mercenaries.
Tutsi-led rebels who took up arms against the Zaire army last October have seized a long border strip in eastern Zaire and seized many important towns.
They said their next target is Kisangani, where President Mobutu Seseko has based his so far ineffective mercenary-backed counter-offensive.
More than a million Hutus who fled violence in Burundi and Rwanda in 1993 and 1994 were initially trapped by the fighting. More than half that number returned to Rwanda late last year.
